## The Mass Gap: Thorin Measures, Brownian Motion and Yang Mills

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 97 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [The Mass Gap: Thorin Measures, Brownian Motion and Yang Mills](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). A probabilistic study of the Yang Mills mass gap: Thorin measures, Brownian motion on SU(2) and the Migdal Kadanoff ladder, with proofs that the projected ladder contracts at every coupling and that the reciprocal heat kernel is a generalized gamma convolution. The four dimensional gap stays open. Keywords: Yang Mills mass gap, reflection positivity, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, Brownian motion on SU(2), heat kernel, Migdal Kadanoff renormalization, lattice gauge theory, Lee Yang zeros, Kingman coalescent, Markov chain Monte Carlo, Bayesian computation.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24546905): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24546905 for version 1.0.0; the BibTeX entry is on the book page

- [Main result: Hypergeometric law of coalescence](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#coalescence_is_hypergeometric): Theorem 9.4, page 141, proved. The coalescence kernel of the SU(2) convolution ladder is the hypergeometric law of the overlap of two random subsets, and its positivity is the Chu Vandermonde identity.
- [Main result: Harmonic law for the mean count of a convolution](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#harmonic_law): Theorem 9.8, page 147, proved. Under convolution the mean counts combine like resistances in parallel, with an explicit constant correction and an error of order one over the smallest index.
- [Main result: First rung theorem for laws with real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#first_rung_theorem): Theorem 9.13, page 150, proved. For link laws in the class with real zeros, one exact ladder rung changes the mean count by a constant depending only on the ratio of variance to mean, with explicit limits for point masses and Wilson laws; the heat kernel value is not proved.
- [Main result: Real zeros are preserved by convolution and heat flow on SU(2)](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#real_zeros_under_convolution): Theorem 10.4, page 164, proved. Convolution of class functions on SU(2) preserves real zeros beyond the edge of the group when one factor has such an antiderivative, and heat flow preserves the class of link densities with real zeros.
- [Main result: Thorin form of the Hartman Watson law](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#thorin_form_hartman_watson): Theorem 10.7, page 168, proved. The Hartman Watson law is a generalized gamma convolution with no drift, and its Thorin distribution function is minus the phase of the Bessel function of imaginary order divided by pi.
- [Main result: Product formula for the SU(2) heat kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#product_formula): Theorem 13.1, page 213, proved. The SU(2) heat kernel is a product of linear factors in cos theta whose real roots all lie beyond the edge of the group and move monotonically in time.
- [Main result: The projected ladder contracts at every coupling](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#the_ladder_contracts): Corollary 13.17, page 235, proved. For the heat kernel projection of the Migdal Kadanoff map the coupling strictly decreases at every rung, for every coupling and scale factor in four dimensions.
- [Main result: Thorin form of the SU(2) heat kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/mass_gap/results.html#heat_kernel_thorin_form): Corollary 13.4, page 214, proved. The reciprocal of the SU(2) heat kernel, as a function of the cosine of the angle, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution with unit atoms at the roots of the product formula.
